title: Hubble spots a celestial bauble
caption: The supernova remnant SNR 0509-67.5, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: SNR B0509-67.5 · constellation Dorado · about 150000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA). Acknowledgement: J. Hughes (Rutgers University)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A delicate shell seems to drift calmly through space in this Hubble image, but the calm is misleading. This bubble, SNR B0509-67.5 or SNR 0509 for short, is what remains visible of a mighty stellar blast in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a small galaxy roughly 160 000 light-years away.

The gaseous shell formed as the expanding blast wave and debris from the supernova tore through the surrounding interstellar gas. It measures 23 light-years across and is growing at more than 18 million kilometers per hour.

Ripples run across the shell's surface. They may come from small variations in the density of the surrounding gas, or they may be pushed from inside by fragments of the original explosion. The caption leaves both possibilities open.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (1.23 x 0.95 arcminutes) and distance (150000 light years), the frame spans roughly 54 × 41 light-years. Its light set out about 150,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This combines a hydrogen-alpha image of the shell from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys with visible and near-infrared images of the star field from Wide Field Camera 3. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The faint glowing shell would be invisible by eye, and part of the star-field data is near-infrared.

explore: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed the remnant on 28 October 2006 using a filter that isolates the light of glowing hydrogen in the shell. Those data were combined with visible-light images of the surrounding stars taken by Wide Field Camera 3 on 4 November 2010.
alt: A delicate, bubble-shaped shell of gas with rippled edges floating among stars.
